draft.title: Imprisonment
card: Imprisonment is a sanction that removes the offender from the community and holds them in a prison. It is the most serious sanction a court in Victoria can impose.
Courts treat it as a last resort. A judge or magistrate considers whether a less serious sanction, such as a fine or a community correction order, could meet the purposes of sentencing.
Imprisonment can punish the offender and protect the community, because the offender cannot reoffend in the community while held. It can also deter others and denounce the crime.
It has limits. The offender may lose a job, housing and family contact, which can make returning to the community harder. Rehabilitation programs in prison may help, but this is not certain.
draft.remember: Imprisonment is the most serious sanction, used when less serious sanctions would not be enough.

a.q: What does it mean to say imprisonment is a last resort?
opts: Less serious sanctions are considered before it is imposed
It can only be imposed after an offender has reoffended
It is only used for offences that involve violence
It is chosen when the offender cannot pay a fine
a.why: A last resort means a court asks whether a less serious sanction could meet the purposes of sentencing before it chooses prison. It does not depend on reoffending or on violence, as the card does not limit it to those cases.
a.clue: Think about what a court looks at first.

b.q: Tariq is sentenced to prison for a serious offence. The judge says the community needs protection from him. Which purpose of sanctions does imprisonment mainly serve here?
opts: Protecting the community by removing him from it
Rehabilitating him by keeping him in his job
Punishing him by letting him stay with his family
Denouncing the crime by ordering unpaid work
b.why: Prison removes the offender from the community, so he cannot reoffend there while held. The other options describe things prison does not do: it does not keep a person in a job or with family, and unpaid work is a community correction order condition.
b.clue: Where is the offender while serving the sanction?

a.best: Less serious sanctions are considered before it is imposed

b.best: Protecting the community by removing him from it

problems.detail: The stem says the judge wants the community protected, and only one option begins 'Protecting the community'. A student can match the words without knowing the idea.

Each distractor pairs a purpose with something prison plainly does not do (staying with family, unpaid work, keeping a job). They contradict the stem's own fact that Tariq is in prison, so the question is far too easy for Year 11 and does not test understanding of the purposes of imprisonment.

check.summary: The card and question a are accurate. Question b gives its answer away: the right option repeats the stem's wording about protecting the community, and the distractors contradict the fact that Tariq is in prison.

a.q: What does it mean to say imprisonment is a last resort?
opts: Less serious sanctions are considered before it is imposed
It can only be imposed after an offender has reoffended
It is only used for offences that involve violence
It is chosen when the offender cannot pay a fine
a.why: A last resort means a court first asks whether a less serious sanction could meet the purposes of sentencing. Prison is not limited to repeat offenders or violent crimes, and it is not a simple backup for an unpaid fine.
a.clue: Think about what a court looks at first.

b.q: Tariq has seriously assaulted two people. The judge wants to stop him harming anyone for the next few years and sends him to prison. What best explains how prison achieves this aim?
opts: He cannot offend in the community while he is held
The sentence warns others that the crime leads to prison
The sentence shows the public disapproves of his crime
Prison programs are sure to change his behaviour
b.why: While Tariq is held, he cannot reoffend in the community, so people are protected for the length of his sentence. Warning others is deterrence and showing disapproval is denunciation: both are real purposes, but neither stops Tariq himself. Rehabilitation in prison may help, but it is not certain.
b.clue: Which option is about Tariq himself, during his sentence?

a.best: Less serious sanctions are considered before it is imposed

b.best: He cannot offend in the community while he is held
